summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would correct drafting and clerical errors across Commonwealth legislation, update technical language and repeal provisions and Acts that are spent or obsolete.
It would fix cross-references, numbering and misdescribed amendments, and replace redundant provisions with references to the general interpretation and legislative instruments frameworks.
Many corrections would start on Royal Assent, with some retrospective provisions aligned to earlier amendments and safeguards maintaining the validity of existing acting appointments.
changes: Redundant acting-appointment validity provisions would be removed where general interpretation law already deals with them.
Social security cross-references would be corrected to point to the intended provisions.
Amendments incorrectly identifying their target provisions would be repaired.
Obsolete Acts and provisions would be repealed without changing the substance of the law.
summary.affected: Commonwealth and private publishers of legislation, and acting appointees covered by the saving provisions, are affected.

speeches.speaker: Michael Keenan
speeches.brief: Supported the Statute Law Revision Bill 2012, describing it as a noncontroversial measure that corrects drafting and clerical errors, repeals obsolete legislation and updates redundant provisions, including air passenger ticket levy acts discontinued in 2003.

speeches.speaker: Michelle Rowland
speeches.brief: Supported the Statute Law Revision Bill 2013, arguing that correcting errors, redundant provisions, punctuation, references and drafting improves the accessibility and reliability of Commonwealth legislation, and highlighting plain-language guidance and a telecommunications law iPad app as examples of legal accessibility.

speeches.speaker: Shayne Neumann
speeches.brief: Commended the Statute Law Revision Bill 2013 for correcting minor errors, repealing obsolete provisions and improving the accuracy, clarity and usability of Commonwealth legislation across areas including telecommunications, corporations law, aviation, native title, superannuation and transport.
